title: Absolute file evidence resolves to its DEEPEST containing worktree, canonicalized, by exact path segment
context: dec_d09ab8e9a0 (now corrected/extended here) generalized the misroute guard's existence check to compare an absolute file-evidence entry directly against each candidate directory via relative(dir, f), rather than relativizing against root first. A THIRD independent MR review (mr-complexity-reviewer, PR #76 round 3) verified by execution that this still had three false-negative shapes, one reproduced end-to-end through the real MCP server with nothing written and a silent commit to the wrong root: (a) a NESTED worktree (root/.worktrees/feature -- the exact layout `hunch worktree` itself creates) is lexically under root's own directory tree, so the plain 'is f under root' check wrongly attributed a file that exists only in the nested worktree to root, short-circuiting before the candidate loop ever ran; (b) a worktree reached through a symlinked alias wasn't recognized, since relative() compared raw un-resolved strings; (c) relative()'s return value was checked with rel.startsWith('..'), a STRING PREFIX match, not a path-segment boundary -- a file literally named '..odd.ts' would be wrongly discarded as 'outside the tree'.
decision: Introduced deepestContainer(f, worktrees) in src/mcp/server.ts: for an absolute f, canonicalize both f and every known worktree path (canonicalRootPath -- the same symlink/case resolution resolveActiveRoot already relies on), find every worktree whose tree contains f via a new isWithin(parent, child) segment-boundary check (relative() result is '' or does not start with '..' + path.sep and is not '..' itself -- never a naive string prefix), and pick the LONGEST (most specific) match rather than any containing ancestor. existsUnder(dir, f, worktrees) then asks only 'is dir THE deepest container of f, and does f exist' -- so root never swallows a worktree nested inside it, a symlinked alias resolves to the real worktree, and a literal '..'-prefixed filename is never mistaken for a traversal segment.
consequences: A nested worktree (hunch worktree's own default layout) is now correctly distinguished from its parent root for absolute file evidence -- verified via a real git worktree nested under root, not just reasoned about

A worktree reached through a symlinked alias resolves correctly -- verified with a real symlink fixture (skipped on Windows, where symlink creation needs elevated permissions, matching the guard's existing win32 path-separator conditionals elsewhere in the test suite)

Windows and macOS variants of these paths remain reasoned-about rather than executed: CI's platform-matrix-safety job does not run test/mcproots.test.ts on windows-latest/macos-latest (only parse/io/migrate/matrix-release-verification/team-matrix-e2e do) -- a pre-existing CI-coverage gap, not introduced by this change, and out of scope to fix here
alternatives_rejected: Document the nested-worktree boundary in the guard's doc comment and file a follow-up issue instead of fixing it, the same treatment #75 got -- considered and offered explicitly, but the fix was deterministic (no heuristic false-positive risk, unlike #75's dirty/clean-git-status idea) and already validated against every existing test case, so fixing was cheaper than documenting and tracking a known-missing behavior per this repo's own 'tickets, not TODOs' convention

Keep the naive string-prefix check for the '..' traversal guard since it happened to pass every existing test -- rejected once a concrete counterexample (a file literally named '..odd.ts') was identified; a segment-boundary check costs nothing extra
